scenarios.title: The node under the lamp
scenarios.learning_objective: Select a published node without mistaking a selection for a verdict.
visible_evidence: A bounded graph contains published records.
The selected record remains a reversible view state.
tutorial_guidance: Selection changes what the inspector shows; it does not accuse anyone.
Keep the selection reversible while you gather context.

scenarios.title: The edge with two stories
scenarios.learning_objective: Inspect a relationship and read its direction and provenance before drawing a conclusion.
visible_evidence: A published relationship has source and target records.
The edge carries a relationship family and provenance reference.
tutorial_guidance: An edge is evidence of a relationship, not a confession.
Read direction, time and provenance before you promote a lead.

scenarios.title: The two names in one hat
scenarios.learning_objective: Treat a similarity result as a candidate until the evidence and review justify more.
visible_evidence: The graph exposes published records only.
A candidate may contain agreements, disagreements and missing fields.
tutorial_guidance: Similarity is a lead. It is not an identity verdict.
Keep exact matches, candidates and hard negatives in separate boxes.

scenarios.title: One hop, no heroics
scenarios.learning_objective: Expand only from visible evidence and keep the investigation bounded.
visible_evidence: The initial view is bounded by the case profile.
Expansion accepts an already visible node as its warrant.
tutorial_guidance: A bounded view is a safety rail, not a missing feature.
The warrant is the visible node; hidden evidence stays hidden.

scenarios.title: The biscuit ledger
scenarios.learning_objective: Spend a credit through an idempotent command and keep the ledger replayable.
visible_evidence: The round starts with a published credit budget.
A repeated idempotency key must not debit twice.
tutorial_guidance: A cost belongs to the authoritative action, not to a button click.
Replay the same request and the ledger should remain boring.

scenarios.title: The witness who changed its collar
scenarios.learning_objective: Keep mixed or incomplete evidence in review instead of forcing a clean verdict.
visible_evidence: A contact pair can agree on one field and disagree on another.
A partial evidence set is not a license to invent the missing record.
tutorial_guidance: Contradiction is a state to record, not a nuisance to erase.
Leave the case unresolved when the evidence cannot support a stronger claim.

scenarios.title: The collar that fits
scenarios.learning_objective: Submit a conclusion only after selecting a supported subject and explicit evidence claims.
visible_evidence: The submission form accepts suspect records and evidence claims.
The receipt reports support without exposing protected evaluation data.
tutorial_guidance: A conclusion needs both a subject and a reasoned evidence set.
The receipt is the durable result; the browser is only the messenger.

scenarios.title: The bark in the wrong alley
scenarios.learning_objective: Make an unsupported accusation observable and reversible in the receipt without leaking the protected answer.
visible_evidence: A plausible-looking record can still be unsupported.
The public result reports consequences, not the hidden answer.
tutorial_guidance: The system should make a bad conclusion legible, not silently rewrite it.
A penalty is a game consequence; it is not evidence of culpability.

scenarios.title: The Academy route, end to end
scenarios.learning_objective: Walk the complete tutorial route: observe, investigate, spend, submit and recover the receipt.
visible_evidence: The catalogue owns the case door.
The board owns published evidence and actions.
The resolution owns the immutable receipt.
tutorial_guidance: Every step leaves a typed boundary: screen, action, ledger, result or persistence.
The final proof is a replayable receipt, not a screenshot of a green button.
